answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation anchored to verifiable work history: each agent identity is a vertex in a trust graph, and its standing grows only through attested useful work over time, not free registration. A newcomer starts at the mesa, a flat low-trust plateau, and must climb by completing real tasks peers verify. Sybil identities cannot inherit the relic of past attested work, so an attacker must pay the full cost of building reputation for every fake identity, making mass fakery uneconomic.
